notes:
Context: Lumen Reserve Platforms is an enterprise ecommerce platform embedding conversational search and product personalization into the storefront. Primary ask is a predictable Dedicated pool with throughput guarantees and clear latency SLOs for customer-facing chat. They will likely start with a 6–12 month reserved commitment and evaluate private on-prem pilot for compliance teams.

Key quote: "We need predictable tail latencies — if a promo goes live we can't have customers waiting or falling back to degraded models."

Requirements summary (high level): steady-state chat, high peak bursts (sales events), embedding generation for indexing, reranking for product results. Strict residency requirements for EU PII subsets; corporate legal requires SOC2 + KMS + audit logs before procurement. Very cost-conscious about steady-state unit cost but will pay premium for SLA-backed tail guarantees.

Sizing workshop focused items below (workshop run 2026-03-02): baseline QPS math, tokens/sec baseline and peak multipliers, GPU sizing options (A100/H100), warm pool vs. instant burst planning, fallback routing and auto-fallback policies, and SLA credit language draft. Notes capture the customer's own numbers and Redwood sizing recommendations (see fields).
timeline: 2026-01-15: Intro call (Jordan) — overview of Redwood Dedicated, asked for throughput examples.
2026-02-04: Demo — showed regional routing + canary rollouts; product asked about p95 guarantees.
2026-02-22: Security sync — exchanged SOC2 report and KMS questions; Lumen legal requested retention policy doc (drive link).
2026-03-02: Dedicated sizing workshop (1.5h) — attended by product, infra, security; collected telemetry and spike patterns.
2026-03-08: Follow-up call — discussed draft reserved GPU plan and SLA language; agreed to internal procurement review week of 2026-03-15.
baseline_qps: Steady-state baseline: 35 QPS of chat-like requests (defined as interactive responses where median user turn requests 120 tokens output). This is what product considers baseline for daily active periods.
baseline_tokens_per_sec: Baseline tokens/sec estimate: 35 QPS * 256 average output tokens = ~8,960 tokens/sec steady-state. (Embeddings and reranking accounted separately; embeddings are asynchronous at ~5k calls/day).
peak_vs_steady_summary: Peak multiplier: observed 3–4x spikes during marketing events. Workshop planning used 4x peak assumption (peak QPS ~140, peak tokens/sec ~35,840). Sizing exercise considered 95th percentile sustained peaks for 5–10 minute windows and warm-burst capacity for 30–60s spikes.
desired_latency_slo: Customer target: p95 response latency <= 300ms for short interactive turns (~32 tokens), p95 <= 800ms for full 256-token completions. Require p99 tail crediting and definition (client wants clear credit % per minute below SLO).
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial recommended reservation: 6x H100 80GB equivalents in primary pool sized for steady-state+buffer with 2x H100 warm-burst nodes available for 4x spikes. Alternative: 10x A100 80GB if cost-constrained. Plan includes prefix caching, continuous batching, and KV cache pinning for chat flows to reduce tokens/sec load. Also discussed colocated NVMe cache for on-prem pilot.
sla_negotiations: Customer requires: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated control plane, throughput guarantees for committed pool, defined maintenance windows (48h advance), and financial credits for missed p95/p99 bounds. Redwood to propose credit tiers and a 90-day performance ramp in contract. Data residency and audit logging terms must be attached to SLA.
cost_sensitivity: High: Lumen wants to minimize monthly steady-state spend; prepared to trade some headroom for cost (prefers predictable monthly bill). Open to committed ARR discount in exchange for hard throughput SLOs and reduced per-token pricing on steady-state usage.
